questions.question_text: How does Reginald Arkell use satire and irony to comment on human pretension in 'A Concrete Example'?
questions.correct_answer: Arkell builds anticipation by describing Mrs. Jones's enthusiastic pride in her garden. When the narrator visits, the grand expectation collapses into a pile of cement debris. Through this anti-climax, Arkell gently ridicules how people exaggerate mundane possessions into grand achievements, showing how humor can be derived from ordinary social observations.
